decisions.quote: The current study attempted to replicate the findings of seminal work by Logan and colleagues (1991) and Lively and colleagues (1993), which found that phonetic training with multiple talkers led to greater generalization to novel talkers than single talker training. Across two different measures, our study found no evidence of such effect in a sample of 166 participants. Bayes Factor analyses found that in each case the evidence for a variability benefit was ambiguous.
decisions.reason: The replication was designed to test the central claim that high-variability (multiple-talker) training leads to greater generalization than low-variability (single-talker) training, and found no evidence for this effect across both measures. General pre-to-post learning in both conditions is a baseline check that was also present in the single-talker original and does not make the central replication outcome mixed.

corrected_value.title: Training Japanese listeners to identify English /r/ and /l/. II: The role of phonetic environment and talker variability in learning new perceptual categories
corrected_value.authors: Lively, S. E., Logan, J. S., & Pisoni, D. B.

decisions.quote: The goal of the current paper is to replicate the key experiments from Logan et al. (1991) and Lively et al. (1993) and test the hypothesis that using high variability input (specifically, input with multiple talkers) leads to more generalisation in phonetic learning than when low variability input is used.
decisions.reason: The study explicitly re-tests both the multiple-talker experiment from Logan et al. (1991) and the single-talker experiment (Experiment 2) from Lively et al. (1993) to evaluate the high- versus low-variability contrast; Lively et al. (1993) is an independent original paper omitted from the shipped rows, with a failed replication outcome.

parent_objection: Additional source context immediately after the first quote says: This means that null effects are not established but also indicates that this type of training paradigm is not sufficiently sensitive to detect variability benefits. Inspect the full final Conclusion and discussion of power/sensitivity. Does the authors substantive verdict say this attempt cannot provide a meaningful test,supporting uninformative under the codebook,or is this only cautious/imprecise evidence alongside an overall failed replication verdict? Do not infer uninformative from Bayes-factor ambiguity or nonsignificance alone; resolve whether their stated insufficient sensitivity is a defect of this attempt that precludes adjudication. The core claim and both Logan1991/Lively1993 target identities remain accepted; general learning baseline does not make mixed. Settle the outcome for both the shippedLogan row and confirmed omittedLively target; return that existing target object with supported outcome,not a new identity.

shipped.title_o: Training Japanese listeners to identify English /r/ and /l/: A first report
shipped.outcome_quote: We find that listeners learn in both multiple and single talker conditions. However, in training, we find no difference in how well listeners learn for high vs low variability training.
